institutionName: Institut d'Etudes Politiques de Toulouse (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I knew I wanted to go to France and I chose the city closest to my French family.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: On a personal level it was an amazing and very giving semester. Academically it wasn't thaaat impressive but luckily that's not the reason I chose to go :)

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The administration at Toulouse was very helpful but some things were a bit unnecessarily complicated so I had to  them a lot of questions

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The administration at Toulouse had an info meeting

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was really stressed about housing because I wanted to find something before arriving in the city. I ended up finding something through a website that's kind of like airbnb but for sharing flats over a longer period of time. It worked fine but I paid too much compared to what I got for the money. Looking back at it now I shouldn't have stressed about it so much and maybe have gone there a bit earlier to look at the places before choosing where to live..

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Most people live off campus so don't stress about it if you don't get any housing on campus

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's not that it was difficult per se but in general I think there's waaaayy too much unnecessary bureaucratic stuff to do when going on exchange

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: To be honest I can't really remember right now and I'm not exactly sure what KU asked for and what Toulouse asked for but in general just sending loaaads of documents and emails back and forth

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Toulouse has and international office that's very helpful and answers mails quickly! It's also possible to call them by phone.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Quite successful because I was fast. At first they wouldn't let me take courses from both the french and english track (you're only allowed to take 2 courses from the track you're not on) but because I needed them for my forhåndsgodkendelse at KU they accepted at the end but I had to a lot of pressure in order for it to be allowed :)

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to sign up for classes as soon as possible

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: To be honest I wasn't very impressed by the academic part of my exchange. I think a lot of it is because of the classes and the teachers I have but in general the system is just very different. A lot of listening and learning by heart and not so much critical thinking and participation (at least in the classes I had - I've heard it was the opposite in some of the other classes...

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It felt a lot like being back in high school...

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot of listening and learning by heart. No breaks in classes and not so much participation of the students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Courses taken in French:
- Sociologie des conflits (master programme) (5 ECTS)
- Négociations et lobbying européen (master programme) (5 ECTS)
- Institutions européennes (5 ECTS)
- Culture et civilisation francaises (4 ECTS)

Courses taken in English:
- Contemporary Political Debates in the UK (5 ECTS)
- Political Regime of France (5 ECTS)
- Central Asian Politics and Society (5 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked Contemporary Political Debates in the UK but I think the courses that they offer change a lot from semester to semester

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I wouldn't say it's an unexpected cost but I travelled a lot in the weekends so that's why my personal spending per months is so high. I also bought a bike which is why the local transportations is so high but you can rent city bikes really cheap which I maybe should've done instead if I wanted to spend less money

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: My housing was more expensive that planned but if I hadn't stressed about it as much I would've been able to find something better and cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There's A LOT of erasmus people in Toulouse so loads of activities all the time. Sciences Po also has loads of clubs and societies.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Loads of different clubs ans societies - both creative, cultural, sports, politics etc etc

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Just join any cub you find interesting

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hiking in the Pyrenees!! Once on a day trip and once where we stayed from friday to sunday. I didn't have classes on monday or friday so I went on loads od weekend trips (Bordeaux, Montpellier, Paris, Marseille)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I'm half french so I thought it was very easy :)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Learn french and don't be afraid to just talk to them. They're friendlier than they may seem ;)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I'm half french so I didn't really think of the cultural differences that much...

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How the cafes and bars are full every night - no matter if it's saturday or tuesday

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Don't go there purely for academic reasons - you'll learn so much from going but probably not the most from an academic point of view
- Don't take the first housing you get offered if it isn't the greatest
- Explore the rest of France while you're there as well

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Enjoy it, it's gonna be great!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being close to my french family and meeting lovely people from all over

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting my forhåndsgodkendelse etc accepted

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: There's gonna be loads of bureaucratic stuff to deal with but it'll sort itself out eventually :))

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
